title: Up in Order, Down in Reverse: Bringing a Graph of Nodes Up and Rolling It Back

questions.question: Why not start every node at once and let them find each other?
options: The robot works when the machine is fast and fails when it is not, and when one node does not come up the others are left running without it
questions.explanation: Start up order decided by timing is luck.

questions.question: Planner, controller, filter, driver, logger and viewer are listed in that order, each needing the one it follows in the chain. What is the start order?
options: driver filter planner controller logger viewer: every node after what it needs, ties going to the one listed first
questions.explanation: The choice depends on nothing but the list.

questions.question: What does a circle of needs do to the start order?
options: The list is refused with the reason: a needing b needing c needing a has no start order
questions.explanation: Finding out by trying would be a robot that hangs at start up.

questions.question: Why configure every node before activating any?
options: Nothing produces until it is known that everything which consumes it exists, so a failed configure has not yet sent a single message
questions.explanation: Configure opens devices and can fail; activate makes it run.

questions.question: The planner will not configure. What does the log show?
options: driver:configure filter:configure planner:configure filter:cleanup driver:cleanup: the ones that did configure are cleaned up in reverse and nothing was activated

questions.question: An optional logger fails and a plotter needs it. What is running?
options: Driver, filter and controller: logger and plotter are left out, and the report says which were skipped
questions.explanation: A degraded robot is up, and says so.
